assets.title: What is geometrical optics?
assets.meaning: Geometrical optics treats light propagation using thin rays by neglecting the finite wavelength of light when apertures are large.

assets.title: What is optical path length?
assets.meaning: Optical path length is the integral of refractive index n along the geometric path, equal to c times the travel time.

assets.title: What is Fermat's principle?
assets.meaning: Fermat's principle states that the actual ray path between two points makes the optical path length stationary with respect to small path variations.

assets.title: Laws of reflection from Fermat's principle
assets.meaning: Reflecting A across mirror MN to A' makes AP + PB = A'P + PB. A straight line A'PB minimizes length, so angle i equals angle r in one plane.

assets.title: What is the paraxial approximation?
assets.meaning: The paraxial approximation assumes rays make very small angles with the optical axis so sine and tangent equal the angle in radians.

assets.title: The Sign Convention at pole P
assets.meaning: Rays are incident from the left. With pole P as origin, distances to the right are positive, to the left are negative, and upward heights are positive.

assets.title: What is a meridional ray?
assets.meaning: A meridional ray is a light ray confined to a single plane containing the optical axis, unlike a non-planar skew ray.

assets.title: What is a thin spherical lens?
assets.meaning: A thin spherical lens is a medium bounded by two spherical refracting surfaces whose thickness t is very small compared to object, image, and curvature distances.

assets.title: Converging and diverging lenses in different media
assets.meaning: For a biconvex lens (R₁ > 0, R₂ < 0), (1/R₁ - 1/R₂) is positive. It converges light when n₂ > n₁, but diverges light when placed in a medium with n₁ > n₂ (Fig. 4.7).

assets.title: What are the first and second principal foci?
assets.meaning: The first principal focus F₁ is the axial object point whose refracted rays emerge parallel (v = ∞), and the second principal focus F₂ is the axial image point for incident parallel rays (u = -∞).

assets.title: Three principal rays for graphical construction
assets.meaning: Ray 1 through F₁ emerges parallel to the axis. Ray 2 parallel to the axis passes through F₂. Ray 3 through lens center P passes undeviated (Fig. 4.8).

assets.title: Measuring object and image from the two foci
assets.meaning: Newton's method measures object distance x₁ from F₁ (positive if right of F₁) and image distance x₂ from F₂ (positive if right of F₂), as in Fig. 4.8.

assets.title: What is lateral magnification?
assets.meaning: Lateral magnification m is the ratio of image height y' to object height y, where positive m means erect and negative m means inverted (Eq. 4.21).

assets.title: What is the superposition principle for sinusoidal waves?
assets.meaning: When two sinusoidal waves of the same frequency superpose in the same direction, their sum x(t) = x₁(t) + x₂(t) is also simple harmonic with the same frequency ω.

assets.title: What are constructive and destructive interference?
assets.meaning: Constructive interference occurs when phase difference is an even multiple of π so a = a₁ + a₂; destructive interference occurs at odd multiples of π so a = |a₁ - a₂|.

assets.title: What is division of wavefront?
assets.meaning: Division of wavefront is a method that divides a single wavefront into two beams using closely spaced holes, slits, mirrors, or a biprism so they keep a fixed phase relationship.

assets.title: What are nodal lines and maxima on a water surface?
assets.meaning: For two in-phase point sources S₁ and S₂, points with path difference nλ form constructive maxima, while points with (n + ½)λ form destructive nodal lines of zero amplitude.

assets.title: What are coherent and incoherent sources?
assets.meaning: Coherent sources maintain a fixed phase relationship over time and form stationary fringes; incoherent sources have a phase difference that varies randomly in ~10⁻¹⁰ s, giving uniform intensity I₁ + I₂.

assets.title: What is fringe width in Young's experiment?
assets.meaning: Fringe width β is the constant distance between any two successive bright or dark fringes on a screen at distance D from two coherent sources separated by d.

assets.title: The cos²(δ/2) intensity distribution (Fig. 14.9)
assets.meaning: For two equal coherent beams, intensity varies as I = 4I₀ cos²(δ/2), reaching maxima 4I₀ at δ = 0, ±2π, ±4π and zero minima at δ = ±π, ±3π, ±5π.

assets.title: What is Fresnel's two-mirror arrangement?
assets.meaning: Fresnel's two-mirror arrangement consists of two plane mirrors M₁M and MM₂ inclined at a small angle θ, producing two coherent virtual images S₁ and S₂ separated by d = 2Rθ.

assets.title: What is Fresnel's biprism?
assets.meaning: Fresnel's biprism is a prism with two very small base angles α (~20') that refracts light from a slit S at distance a into two coherent virtual sources separated by d = 2a(n - 1)α.

assets.title: What is the white-light interference pattern?
assets.meaning: With white light, zero path difference at O produces a white central fringe, flanked by a few colored fringes (reddish then violet) that quickly overlap into uniform white.

assets.title: What is Lloyd's mirror arrangement?
assets.meaning: Lloyd's mirror interferes direct light from slit S₁ with light reflected at grazing incidence from a mirror; its dark central fringe proves a π phase shift on denser reflection.

assets.title: What are Stokes' relations?
assets.meaning: Stokes' relations are t₁t₂ = 1 - r₁² and r₂ = -r₁, derived from optical reversibility for amplitude reflection (r₁, r₂) and transmission (t₁, t₂) coefficients.

assets.title: What is division of amplitude and the cosine law?
assets.meaning: In division of amplitude at a plane parallel film of thickness d and index n₂, the lower reflection travels an extra optical path Δ = 2n₂d cos θ' given by the cosine law.

assets.title: What is a non-reflecting film (blooming)?
assets.meaning: A non-reflecting film is a dielectric layer of index n_f between air (n_a) and glass (n_g) and thickness d = λ/(4n_f) that cancels reflected waves by destructive interference.

assets.title: Reflectivity R(δ) of an anti-reflecting film (Fig. 15.9)
assets.meaning: For n_a = 1, n_g = 1.5, and n_f = √1.5 ≈ 1.225, reflectivity R drops to zero at δ = π/2, 3π/2, 5π/2 (d = λ/4n_f, 3λ/4n_f). A λ/4n_f film is used because R(λ) stays lowest across visible wavelengths.

assets.title: What are fringes of equal thickness and thin-film colors?
assets.meaning: In a thin film of varying thickness illuminated by an extended source, each fringe follows a locus of constant film thickness; white light produces colored fringes if the film is very thin.

objects.text: Constant thickness t along each fringe
objects.name: film

assets.title: What are Newton's rings?
assets.meaning: Newton's rings are concentric dark and bright circular fringes formed by interference in the thin air film between a plano-convex lens of radius R and a plane glass plate.

assets.title: What is the Michelson interferometer?
assets.meaning: The Michelson interferometer uses a 45° beam splitter G₁, compensating plate G₂, and perpendicular mirrors M₁ and M₂ to form circular fringes of equal inclination with path difference 2d cos θ.

assets.title: What is Fraunhofer diffraction at a single slit?
assets.meaning: Fraunhofer diffraction occurs when source and screen are effectively at infinity using lenses. A plane wave hitting a slit of width b excites n point sources of spacing Δ that send parallel rays at angle θ to P.

assets.title: What is the single-slit diffraction pattern?
assets.meaning: The single-slit pattern has a central maximum I = I₀ at θ = 0 (since sin β/β → 1), dark minima I = 0 at b sin θ = mλ (m = ±1, ±2, …), and weak secondary maxima at the roots of tan β = β.

assets.title: Single-slit intensity distribution I = I₀(sin²β/β²) (Fig. 18.4)
assets.meaning: The central maximum at β = 0 reaches I₀, flanked by zero minima at β = ±π, ±2π, ±3π. Secondary maxima at roots of tan β = β (β = ±1.43π, ±2.46π) have heights 4.96% and 1.68% of I₀.

assets.title: What is the two-slit Fraunhofer diffraction pattern?
assets.meaning: The two-slit Fraunhofer pattern of two parallel slits (width b, separation d) has intensity equal to the product of the single-slit diffraction factor (sin²β/β²) and the two-source interference factor (cos²γ).

assets.title: What are maxima, minima, and missing orders in two-slit diffraction?
assets.meaning: Diffraction minima occur at b sin θ = mλ (m = 1, 2, …) and interference minima at d sin θ = (n + ½)λ. Missing orders occur when an interference maximum d sin θ = nλ coincides with a diffraction minimum b sin θ = mλ.

objects.text: Missing order at sin θ = mλ/b = nλ/d
objects.name: env

assets.title: Double-slit intensity distribution with missing order (Fig. 18.31)
assets.meaning: For d = 4b, rapid cos²(4β) interference fringes sit inside the sin²β/β² diffraction envelope. The n = ±4 interference maxima fall on the m = ±1 diffraction minima at β = ±π and are missing (circled).

assets.title: What are principal maxima and secondary minima in N-slit diffraction?
assets.meaning: For N slits of width b and spacing d, principal maxima occur at γ = mπ (d sin θ = mλ) with intensity N²I₀(sin²β/β²). Between adjacent principal maxima lie (N - 1) secondary minima and (N - 2) weak secondary maxima.

assets.title: N-slit interference factor sin²(Nγ)/sin²γ for N = 5 (Fig. 18.33)
assets.meaning: For N = 5 slits, sharp principal maxima of height N² = 25 occur at γ = 0, ±π, ±2π. Between consecutive principal maxima lie N - 1 = 4 secondary minima (at γ = pπ/5) and N - 2 = 3 weak secondary maxima.

assets.title: What is a diffraction grating and its angular dispersion?
assets.meaning: A diffraction grating has N equidistant slits of grating element d. Its principal maxima satisfy d sin θ = mλ (zeroeth order m = 0 is undispersed white), and its angular dispersion is Δθ/Δλ = m/(d cos θ).

assets.title: What is the resolving power of a diffraction grating?
assets.meaning: The resolving power R = λ/Δλ of a grating is its power to distinguish two nearby spectral lines λ and λ + Δλ. By the Rayleigh criterion, R equals the product of diffraction order m and total exposed lines N.

objects.text: d sin θ = m(λ+Δλ) = mλ + λ/N
objects.name: common

assets.title: What are Fresnel half-period zones?
assets.meaning: Fresnel half-period zones are annular rings on a plane wavefront bounded by circles at distances d + nλ/2 from P. Each zone has radius r_n ≈ √(nλd), equal area πλd, and is π out of phase with its neighbours.

assets.title: What is the Poisson spot and circular-aperture axial diffraction?
assets.meaning: A circular hole of radius a gives axial maxima for odd numbers of zones (1st zone alone gives u₁ and intensity 4I₀) and minima for even numbers of zones. An opaque disc blocking p zones always leaves u_{p+1}/2, forming a bright Poisson spot.

assets.title: What is a Fresnel zone plate?
assets.meaning: A zone plate consists of concentric circles of radii r_n = √n K with alternate annular zones blackened. For an incident plane wave, it forms an intense primary focus at f = K²/λ and weaker foci at K²/(3λ), K²/(5λ), …

assets.title: What are the Fresnel integrals and Cornu's spiral?
assets.meaning: Fresnel integrals C(τ) = ∫₀^τ cos(πu²/2)du and S(τ) = ∫₀^τ sin(πu²/2)du are odd functions with C(0)=S(0)=0 and C(∞)=S(∞)=1/2. Their parametric plot is Cornu's spiral, whose chord length gives wave amplitude.

assets.title: What is the straight-edge Fresnel diffraction pattern?
assets.meaning: For a plane wave incident on a straight edge at distance d from the screen, intensity is I₀/4 on the shadow edge (y = 0), decays monotonically to 0 in the shadow (y < 0), and oscillates (peaking at 1.37 I₀) for y > 0.

assets.title: Universal straight-edge intensity curve I/I₀ (Fig. 20.13)
assets.meaning: Plotted against √(2/λd) y = -v₀, intensity is 0.25 I₀ at y = 0, drops smoothly to 0 in the shadow (y < 0), and oscillates in the lit region with maxima 1.37 I₀ (-v₀ ≈ 1.22), 1.20 I₀ (2.34), and first minimum 0.778 I₀ (1.87).

assets.title: What are linearly and circularly polarised waves?
assets.meaning: In a linearly (plane) polarised wave, vibrations stay on one line in the x-z or y-z plane. In a circularly polarised wave, each point moves on a circle of radius a.

assets.title: What is unpolarised light and a Polaroid pass axis?
assets.meaning: In unpolarised light, the transverse electric vector E changes direction randomly. A Polaroid absorbs E along one axis and transmits E along its perpendicular pass axis.

assets.title: What are a wire-grid polariser and a Polaroid?
assets.meaning: A wire-grid polariser has parallel wires spaced less than λ that absorb E parallel to the wires by Joule heating and transmit E perpendicular. A Polaroid uses aligned iodine polymer chains.

assets.title: What is Brewster's law?
assets.meaning: Brewster's law states that when unpolarised light hits an interface at θ_p = tan⁻¹(n₂/n₁), the reflected ray is linearly polarised perpendicular to the plane of incidence and is 90° to the refracted ray.

assets.title: What are dichroism, a Nicol prism, and scattering polarisation?
assets.meaning: Dichroism is selective absorption of one polarised beam (as in tourmaline). A Nicol prism uses Canada balsam to remove the ordinary ray by total internal reflection. Gas scattering at 90° is also linearly polarised.

assets.title: What is Malus's law?
assets.meaning: Malus's law states that when a linearly polarised beam of intensity I₀ falls on an analyser whose pass axis makes an angle θ with the incident electric vector, the emergent intensity is I = I₀ cos²θ.

assets.title: What are crossed polarisers and how does rotation change intensity?
assets.meaning: Crossed polarisers have perpendicular pass axes (θ = 90°), giving zero transmitted intensity. Rotating one Polaroid through 360° produces two maxima (0°, 180°) and two zero minima (90°, 270°).

assets.title: Malus's law intensity curve I = I₀ cos²θ
assets.meaning: As analyser angle θ varies from 0 to 2π, transmitted intensity I = I₀ cos²θ reaches maxima I₀ at θ = 0, π, 2π, equals 0.5 I₀ at θ = π/4, and drops to zero at θ = π/2 and 3π/2.

assets.title: What are double refraction, the ordinary ray, and the extraordinary ray?
assets.meaning: Double refraction is the splitting of light in an anisotropic crystal into two linearly polarised rays: the ordinary ray (o-ray, obeys Snell's law, D ⊥ optic axis) and extraordinary ray (e-ray, D in optic-axis plane).

assets.title: What are the optic axis, negative crystals, and positive crystals?
assets.meaning: The optic axis is the direction in a uniaxial crystal where o-ray and e-ray speeds equal c/n_o. In negative crystals (calcite, n_e < n_o) the e-ellipsoid lies outside the o-sphere; in positive (n_e > n_o) inside.

assets.title: Huygens' construction for normal and oblique incidence (Figs. 22.23–22.25)
assets.meaning: Huygens' construction draws spheres of radius c/n_o (tangent OO' → o-ray BO) and ellipsoids of axes c/n_o, c/n_e (tangent EE' → e-ray BE). If the optic axis is parallel to the surface, both travel along BO.

assets.title: What is a quarter-wave plate (QWP)?
assets.meaning: A quarter-wave plate is a uniaxial crystal plate with its optic axis parallel to the surface whose thickness d introduces a phase difference of π/2 (or (2m+1)π/2, path difference λ₀/4) between o- and e-waves.

assets.title: What is a half-wave plate (HWP)?
assets.meaning: A half-wave plate is a crystal plate with optic axis parallel to the surface that introduces a phase difference of π (path difference λ₀/2). It rotates linear polarisation at angle φ by 2φ and flips LCP to RCP.

assets.title: What is the procedure for analysis of polarised light?
assets.meaning: Rotating a Polaroid gives extinction for linear light, constant intensity for unpolarised or circular light, and partial variation for elliptical or mixed light. Adding a QWP distinguishes circular and elliptical states.

assets.title: What is optical activity?
assets.meaning: Optical activity is the rotation of the plane of polarisation by φ(z) = (π/λ)(n_L - n_R)z because LCP and RCP modes have different indices n_L and n_R. Dextro-rotatory media have n_L > n_R; laevo-rotatory have n_L < n_R.
